answers.question: How many sparsity rates have at least one bar (either Per-Output or Per-Layer) with a perplexity value above 100?
answers.reasoning: Only at 80% sparsity do the bars jump well above 10^2 (100) on the log-scale y-axis; all sparsity rates up to 70% stay below 100.

answers.reasoning: The Per-Layer vs Per-Output gap is smallest at 40% (nearly equal), slightly larger at 50%, and clearly larger at 60% (orange notably above blue).

answers.question: Does the gap between the Per-Layer and Per-Output configurations widen as sparsity rate increases, and if so, at which sparsity rates is this most pronounced?
answers.answer: Yes; most pronounced at 70% and especially 80%
answers.reasoning: From 10% to 60% the two bars are close, but at 70% the orange bar rises to roughly double the blue, and at 80% both increase sharply with a large separation (Per-Layer much higher).
